hook: Douglas Hofstadter was born in New York City in 1945, the son of Nobel physicist Robert Hofstadter, and earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics from Stanford in 1965 before completing a Ph.D. in physics at the University of Oregon in 1975. In 1979 he published Godel, Escher, Bach: An Eternal Golden Braid, a book weaving mathematical logic, art, and music to argue that self-reference and recursive pattern-matching underlie meaning and mind, and it won the Pulitzer Prize for General Nonfiction in 1980. He joined Indiana University Bloomington, where he directed the Fluid Analogies Research Group and became a Distinguished Professor of Cognitive Science and Comparative Literature, building computer models of analogy-making such as Copycat with his students. His later book I Am a Strange Loop (2007) restated the argument that consciousness itself is a kind of self-referential loop. Across four decades he has argued that genuine intelligence rests on fluid analogy-making, a position that put him at odds with mainstream symbolic and, more recently, statistical approaches to AI.

quick_facts: Born in New York City in 1945, the son of Nobel Prize-winning physicist Robert Hofstadter
Earned a B.S. in mathematics from Stanford in 1965 and a Ph.D. in physics from the University of Oregon in 1975
Won the Pulitzer Prize for General Nonfiction and the American Book Award in 1980 for Godel, Escher, Bach
Directed the Fluid Analogies Research Group and its Copycat program modeling analogy-making
Distinguished Professor of Cognitive Science and Comparative Literature at Indiana University Bloomington
Wrote the Metamagical Themas column for Scientific American from 1981 to 1983

achievements.title: Godel, Escher, Bach: An Eternal Golden Braid (1979)
achievements.impact: Argued that self-reference and recursive pattern-matching, illustrated through Godel's incompleteness theorems, Escher's art, and Bach's fugues, are a common root of meaning and mind. Won the 1980 Pulitzer Prize for General Nonfiction.

achievements.title: Fluid Analogies Research Group and Copycat
achievements.impact: Built computer programs that model analogy-making on letter-string puzzles, arguing analogy, not search or logic, is the core mechanism of thought.

achievements.title: I Am a Strange Loop (2007)
achievements.impact: Extended the strange-loop argument from Godel, Escher, Bach into a direct theory of consciousness as self-referential pattern.

achievements.title: Metamagical Themas (Scientific American, 1981-1983)
achievements.impact: Popularized ideas from recursion, self-reference, and cognitive science for a broad readership through his monthly column.
